items.prompt: Orthographic top-down architectural plan photograph of a real built film set, taken straight down from high above: camera axis exactly perpendicular to the ground; no wall face, no elevation, no side of any building, wall, hedge or tree trunk is visible; only the ground plane, the top edges of walls and hedges and the tops of trees, furniture and objects are seen. The top of the image is north. Plan of the Queen's croquet-ground, a 60 by 35 metre oblong lawn in an Art Nouveau dream garden after Alphonse Mucha, built as a real set. Along the top (north) edge runs a raised honey-coloured limestone terrace, a narrow pale stone strip across the whole width, its lawn-side edge a carved balustrade seen from above as a thin line of baluster tops; at its centre a flight of stone steps descends to the lawn, and just above the steps on the terrace a crimson canvas awning on a gilded iron frame, seen from above as a crimson rectangle. The left (west), bottom (south) and right (east) sides are closed by tall clipped dark yew hedges, fully present along those edges, seen from above as thick flat-topped green bands, with a rounded arched gap cut through the hedge at the bottom-left corner and another at the bottom-right corner. The whole lawn is heaved into long regular parallel ridges and furrows running left to right, about six gently curving ridges from top to bottom, each ridge lit on one flank and shadowed in the furrow. Two small croquet stakes striped red, white and black stand at the middle of the left end and the middle of the right end. In the bottom-left corner a great cedar of Lebanon, its flat layered plates of dark foliage seen from above, casting a deep pool of shade; at the upper-right edge of that shade a green-and-gold cast-iron garden bench. A strip of herbaceous border in pastel bloom runs inside the hedges. No hoops, no balls. Hot low late-afternoon sun from the west (left) rakes across the ridges, long shadows toward the east. The set is empty: no people, no animals, no creatures, no text, no labels, no arrows, no symbols, no map legend. A clean, sharp, evenly exposed photographic plan in which every feature named above is clearly readable in its stated position. Photorealistic live-action fantasy film rooted in England in 1862, shot on 35mm film with anamorphic lenses, 16:9 widescreen. Real sets, real locations and real costumed actors in 1862 dress. Wonderland spaces are real built sets and set extensions in an Alphonse Mucha-inspired Art Nouveau design: flowing organic lines, floral and vine ornament, circular halo roundels, mosaic and stained glass, aged pastel-and-gold surfaces with patina and moss; the waking 1862 meadow stays plain period realism. Talking animals and fantastical creatures are photoreal CGI animals with naturalistic anatomy, real fur, feathers, skin and scales, lit by the same light and grounded with real contact shadows. Natural and practical light: sunlight, candlelight and oil lamps, soft haze with volumetric light shafts and soft colour through stained glass. Restrained palette of verdigris teal, slate grey, dusty rose, soft sage and lilac pastels and tarnished-gold accents, warmed by amber sun and candle glow. Fine film grain, gentle halation, soft depth of field, grounded and quietly melancholy.
